steps.note: A five minute talk writes itself about 170 captions and a thousand words. Every press on the timeline used to freeze the app for a sixth to two thirds of a second once they were there (2026-09-24): the menu bar ran a whole Lift on a copy of the document to ask whether Extract could do anything, every caption bar read the whole document as it drew, and a thousand word chips were a thousand views. Each key below is judged on the longest single pass of the main thread after it. On a quiet Mac every one of them takes 20 to 47ms; the walk fails at 80ms, not 50, because the same presses read 30 to 40 percent slower while another window keeps the Mac busy (the dashboard in a browser did, 2026-09-24), and a guard that goes red on a busy machine sends runners after nothing. Every freeze this guards against was 170ms or more.

The captions landing, timed apart from the recording opening: once the window has settled they are taken off and written again the way they write themselves at open, quietly, nothing picked. From the listening starting to the words on the timeline, nothing may hold the main thread for more than 150ms (about 60 to 70ms on a quiet Mac, 90 to 100 on a busy one).
The keys a Premiere editor presses most, each on its own clock: a frame step, the In, zoom in, zoom to fit, and the Out.
